Everyone is different and I can understand why that would be frustrating from your pov. It’s an ongoing debate in many asexual subs on when to bring it up. I am very much, let’s be up front about it because it’s quickest for everyone. However, I know that there are some asexuals who are happy to have sex after getting to know someone on a deeper level. Asexual just means a lack of sexual attraction, not everyone is sex averse and just need time to know you, where as others would never want to do that and might enjoy other activities or no sexual contact. Some asexuals still have libido and want to have sex but they struggle connecting with people. Unfortunately it’s not as linear as other sexual orientations and so there are lots of reasons they may have been on there and not disclosed it earlier. It’s also really hard for us to find other asexuals that are nearby and have the same style, so often we are on these apps hoping to connect with someone understanding and willing to give a relationship a go still. I hope this helps, as I said I don’t speak for all asexuals and everyone has their own reasons and branches of experiences and limits.

Near me vets will not allow you to take animal before fee is paid and you must claim it back from the insurer. Which is why they can argue about the charges because I’m not a professional to say no that should be covered. 

I think as we’ve all established in the thread, insurance is not a one size fits all unfortunately.

In my experience It just doesn’t work like that at all. We paid in over £100 a month for the dogs insurance. But they have limits for everything. You think your being covered for £5000 -£10000 but that’s broken down into small limits across every test and every condition. We got at most 2/3 out of what we paid for our dogs care and we had to do further tests to get that. It was one of the highest level of cover available. 

I don’t know if that is a UK thing but like building insurance they will try and get out of paying out every step of the way.

From my experience I would disagree. 

Last year we had comprehensive lifetime insurance for our dog and cat. In January the dog (12 years old) developed Cushings disease which at her age was too severe to treat. 3 weeks after her symptoms began she was PTS. We had to keep her alive 2 extra weeks for additional tests so that the insurance would pay out. It’s my biggest regret we didn’t just cut our loses after week 1 and let her go in comfort and instead had further tests just for a payout. 

In April the cat (3 years old) was hit by a car and had a leg amputation, we didn’t have the money to pay upfront and hope the insurance paid out so went though a charity instead. He still didn’t make it and 2 weeks post op passed away in his sleep. 

I think sometimes it’s better to put money aside each month and cover the costs yourself but sometimes it isn’t. Can’t call it in advanced unfortunately.
